speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly how long you've been experiencing this itchy rash and the numbness on your palms? Also, have you noticed if the rash appears anywhere else on your body or if the tingling spreads to your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if you were bitten by any insects, such as ticks or chiggers, while working on the rice farm or around the livestock? Also, has the rash changed in appearance, for instance, becoming scaly or forming blisters?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your symptoms of eyebrow and eyelash loss along with hypopigmented macules, do you have any history of contact with someone diagnosed with leprosy, or have you noticed any thickening of the nerve trunks on your body? I will now request a skin biopsy and nerve conduction studies to confirm our suspicion. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy; REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Biopsy: Chronic inflammatory cells with features suggestive of leprosy; Nerve_Conduction_Studies: Reduced sensory nerve action potentials in the ulnar nerves; Serology: Anti-PGL-1_antibodies Positive; Vital_Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood_Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart_Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory_Rate 14 breaths/min; Skin_Examination: Multiple erythematous macules and papules on face, arms, chest, and back; Hypopigmented macules around elbows with insensitivity to light touch, temperature, and pinprick; Slight reduction in bilateral grip strength; Loss of eyebrow and eyelash hairs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results, including the positive Anti-PGL-1 antibodies and skin biopsy findings, combined with your specific symptoms of eyebrow loss and insensitive hypopigmented patches, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Borderline Tuberculoid Leprosy.
